purpose: Configure rules, view status, manage the kernel audit subsystem

sections.title: Status
sections.code:
auditctl -s                    # Show current status (enabled, pid, backlog, etc.)
auditctl -l                    # List all loaded rules
auditctl -e 1                  # Enable auditing
auditctl -e 0                  # Disable auditing
auditctl -e 2                  # Make configuration immutable (until reboot)

sections.title: Clear / load
sections.code:
auditctl -D                    # Delete all rules
auditctl -R /etc/audit/audit.rules   # Load rules from a file

sections.title: Buffer & failure mode
sections.code:
auditctl -b 8192               # Set backlog buffer size
auditctl -f 1                  # Failure mode: 0=silent, 1=printk, 2=panic

sections.title: File watches
sections.code:
auditctl -w /etc/passwd -p wa -k identity
auditctl -w /etc/shadow -p rwa -k sensitive
auditctl -W /etc/passwd        # Remove a watch

sections.title: Syscall rules
sections.code:
auditctl -a always,exit -F arch=b64 -S execve -k process_creation
auditctl -a always,exit -F arch=b64 -S open,openat -F exit=-EACCES -k access_denied
auditctl -d always,exit -F arch=b64 -S execve -k process_creation   # Delete a rule

sections.title: Useful filters
sections.code:
-F auid>=1000
-F auid!=unset
-F uid=0
-F euid!=uid
-F path=/usr/bin/sudo
-F exit=-EPERM
-F key=mykey

notes: Permission flags for -p: r = read, w = write, x = execute, a = attribute change

purpose: Search and display events from the audit logs

sections.title: By time
sections.code:
ausearch -ts today
ausearch -ts recent                   # Last 10 minutes
ausearch -ts 10:00:00 -te 11:00:00
ausearch -ts 01/15/2025

sections.title: By user / process
sections.code:
ausearch -ua 1000                     # auid
ausearch -ui 0                        # uid
ausearch -ul root                     # login name
ausearch -p 12345                     # pid
ausearch -pp 1234                     # ppid

sections.title: By syscall / success
sections.code:
ausearch -sc execve
ausearch -sc open,openat
ausearch -sv yes                      # success=yes
ausearch -sv no                       # success=no

sections.title: By message type
sections.code:
ausearch -m SYSCALL
ausearch -m USER_AUTH,USER_LOGIN
ausearch -m AVC

sections.title: Output formats
sections.code:
ausearch -k identity -i               # Interpret
ausearch -k identity --raw            # Raw
ausearch -k identity -i -c cat        # Interpret + command name filter
ausearch -k identity --format csv
ausearch -k identity --format text

purpose: Generate summary reports from the audit logs

sections.title: Reports
sections.code:
aureport                           # Summary report
aureport --summary                 # Overall summary
aureport --auth                    # Authentication report
aureport --login                   # Login report
aureport --file                    # File access report
aureport --executable              # Executable report
aureport --host                    # Host report
aureport --user                    # User report
aureport --terminal                # Terminal report
aureport --key                     # Key report
aureport --syscall                 # Syscall report
aureport --anomaly                 # Anomaly report
aureport --failed                  # Failed events only
aureport --success                 # Successful events only
aureport --start today
aureport --start this-week
aureport -i                        # Interpret numeric values

sections.title: Service management
sections.code:
systemctl status auditd
systemctl start auditd
systemctl stop auditd
systemctl restart auditd           # Note: often requires service auditd restart
service auditd restart             # Preferred on many systems (preserves rules)

sections.title: Signals
sections.code:
kill -TERM $(pidof auditd)         # Clean stop
kill -HUP  $(pidof auditd)         # Reconfigure (reread auditd.conf)
kill -USR1 $(pidof auditd)         # Rotate logs
kill -USR2 $(pidof auditd)         # Resume logging after suspend

sections.title: Compile & load
sections.code:
# Compile /etc/audit/rules.d/*.rules → /etc/audit/audit.rules and load
augenrules --load

# Check syntax without loading
augenrules --check

purpose: Trace a single process like strace, using the audit subsystem

sections.title: Usage
sections.code:
autrace /usr/bin/ls -l /tmp
# Then search the generated events:
ausearch -i -p <pid>
